name: North Dakota
summary: A bald eagle with an olive branch and arrows, holding a scroll reading 'E Pluribus Unum', with 13 stars and a sunburst above and 'North Dakota' on a scroll below, on a blue field with gold fringe. It is based on a regimental flag.
origin: The design copies the flag carried by the 1st North Dakota Infantry in the Spanish–American War and the Philippine–American War. It was adopted in 1911.

symbols.name: Eagle
symbols.description: A bald eagle with a shield of 13 stripes on its breast.

facts: Its proportions, 33:26, make it taller than most flags.
It is nearly identical to the US Army's regimental colours of the period.
clues: A bald eagle with a scroll and stars on blue with gold fringe, and the state name below.
It copies an infantry regiment's flag.
Its proportions are taller than most.
